05 PROJECTS

01 / COMPUTER VISION

FoulVision

FoulVision is a football photo and video analysis application built with YOLO11n (the nano variant of YOLO version 11) and Flask. It highlights contact areas, suspected offending players, and affected players to help referees review incidents and record decisions.

PythonFlaskYOLO11n
More about this project

Model & purpose

Developed from my final-year project, FoulVision uses a YOLO11n object detection model with three classes: foul, fouling_player, and victim. Detections provide visual cues for footage review; the referee makes the final foul decision.

Photo & video input

  • Accepts JPG/PNG photos and MP4 videos through file selection or drag-and-drop, with previews.
  • Limits uploads to 200 MB and videos to 5 minutes, with format and media content checks.
  • Runs analysis in the background with progress indicators and a limited queue.

Annotations & review controls

Output footage displays colored boxes: blue for contact areas, orange for suspected offending players, and green for potentially affected players. Advanced settings let users adjust the confidence threshold, box visibility, and player labels.

Video controls include slow playback, replay from the beginning, and forward and backward frame stepping to review moments of contact more closely.

Decisions & downloads

  • Referees can select Foul, No foul, or Inconclusive, then add notes.
  • Notes are saved in the current browser and can be downloaded as TXT; a note history page is not yet available.
  • Annotated photos and videos can be downloaded. Output videos use H.264 MP4 without audio.
  • A research panel provides detection counts by class, confidence summaries, frames with detections, processing time, and CSV table and JSON summary exports.

Scope of analysis

Videos are analyzed frame by frame, without player tracking or temporal analysis. Detection counts across frames do not represent unique incidents or players. Missing annotations do not establish that no foul occurred. The application is intended for local review; reliability in real matches still needs to be tested with referees.

02 / AI & WEB DEVELOPMENT

Acne Detection

An acne detection and skin type identification application connecting YOLOv8 with a React/Vite interface, a Flask API, and MySQL. Users can run detections, review their history, and generate PDF reports. The project also includes Gemini and WhatsApp integration through Fonnte.

YOLOv8ReactFlaskMySQL
More about this project

Detection & history

The project combines acne detection and skin type identification with user accounts and stored detection history. The documentation shows the home page, detection using a MacBook camera, and a history page for reviewing previous results.

Reports & integrations

Results can be presented in PDF reports. Gemini integration supports optional AI analysis, while Fonnte provides WhatsApp integration. Each service requires its own API configuration before use.

Application architecture

03 / DATA ANALYSIS

Potential Analysis
of Telkomsel Sites

Analysis and Tableau dashboard development to understand network usage patterns and compare the potential of Telkomsel sites. Beginning as an internship project focused on payload, I later expanded it to four categories: payload, digital, games, and video.

PythonPandasNumPyMatplotlibTableau
More about this project

Background & purpose

This project began during my internship at PT Telkomsel Regional Surabaya from March 3 to April 18, 2025. Its aim was to transform daily traffic data into information by site and month that could be explored more easily, supporting usage pattern evaluation and network optimization considerations.

Initial phase — payload analysis

The internship report focused on classifying payload potential into low, medium, and high classes. Daily data was aggregated by site and month, then used for Extra Trees Classifier modeling with PyCaret and Tableau visualizations. Digital, games, and video metrics were already included as supporting features, but the report’s classification target and dashboard focused on payload.

The report recorded processing more than 10.8 million rows of daily data and an Extra Trees evaluation accuracy of 94.03%. This figure is the reported result for the internship-phase payload model, rather than an evaluation of the four-category version or a guarantee of performance on new data.

Latest development — four categories

I expanded the analysis to review payload, digital, games, and video as separate categories. In this version, low, medium, and high classes are defined using separate tertiles of each metric’s daily average per site-month. The results show the relative position of site usage within each category.

Processing workflow & contributions

  • Audited source data and prepared site-month metric aggregates using Python, Pandas, and NumPy.
  • Created classifications for each category, class profiles, and distribution and trend charts with Matplotlib.
  • Prepared analysis outputs and developed a Tableau dashboard for exploring categories, months, and site details.
  • Prepared an insight report, class threshold sensitivity checks, and notes on data limitations.

Latest dashboard features

  • Filters for payload, digital, games, or video categories and month selection.
  • Summaries of site counts, median usage, and the percentage of high-class sites.
  • Site count distribution charts and comparisons of low, medium, and high class profiles.
  • A site detail table with class, average metric values, observation day counts, and calendar coverage.

Results & interpretation

The dashboard helps compare usage characteristics across sites and categories, while the report and supporting charts provide context for historical changes. Potential classes in the latest version describe observed relative usage; they do not predict future demand or establish unmet capacity needs. Differences in observation day coverage and metric definitions should be considered when drawing conclusions.

04 / WEB DEVELOPMENT

Employee Attendance
& Leave

A Flask and SQLite application for leave requests and departure–return attendance, with three roles: admin, manager, and employee. Its workflow covers leave requests, manager decisions, personal QR verification by KASUKI admins, activity history, and configurable WhatsApp notifications.

PythonFlaskSQLite
More about this project

Three user roles

  • Employees submit leave requests, review their personal history, and display departure and return QR codes.
  • Managers review requests assigned to them, approve or reject leave, and monitor its status.
  • Admins manage accounts, units, reporting relationships, and all leave requests. They can also correct data with a reason and a change history.

Leave & QR workflow

Employees enter their destination, purpose, and estimated return time. After approval, they present a personal QR code for KASUKI to confirm their departure. A return QR code becomes available after departure is recorded. Personal QR codes are valid for two minutes, and the application limits each employee to one active leave request.

Monitoring & notifications

The dashboard provides status monitoring, filters, pagination, and CSV exports. Activity history records event timestamps, while WhatsApp integration uses a message queue and Meta’s official WhatsApp Cloud API. Demo mode simulates notifications; actual delivery requires an account, credentials, and approved Meta templates.

Administration & scope

The application includes hashed passwords, login attempt limits, CSRF protection, and SQLite backups through the CLI. Attendance records cover departures and returns associated with leave requests, rather than daily clock-in and clock-out attendance. KASUKI verifies attendance; a QR code does not prove an employee’s physical location.

05 / WEB DEVELOPMENT

Yakes
Medis

A web application for medical records and clinic operations: patient data, doctor schedules, visits and queues, medication catalogs and inventory, examination history, and PDF reports. Built with PHP 8, MySQL, Bootstrap, and Dompdf as a portfolio project using demonstration data. The application supports two user types: admins and doctors.

PHPMySQLBootstrapDompdf
More about this project

Application purpose

Yakes Medis brings medical record keeping and operational data management together in a web application. The project simulates the needs of a small clinic with several departments, allowing patient information, doctor services, visits, and medication supplies to be managed in a structured way.

Users & account access

Yakes Medis supports two user types: admin and doctor.

  • Login, logout, and password changes.
  • User data management through the User module; the documentation includes demo administrator and doctor accounts.

Patients & medical records

  • Create, view, update, and delete data through patient, medication, user, and medical record modules, subject to applicable data relationship constraints.
  • Review patient record history and export medical record reports to PDF with Dompdf.

Doctor schedules & visits

  • View doctors, departments, practice days, service hours, and quotas in the Doctor Schedule menu.
  • Register visits by selecting a department and doctor.
  • Manage visits with unique queue numbers per department per day in the database structure.
  • View an operational dashboard covering patients, visits, queues, completed examinations, and stock requiring attention.

Medication catalog & inventory

  • Manage the medication catalog through the Medication Master module.
  • Monitor stock quantities, units, minimum stock thresholds, and expiration dates through Stock Inventory.
  • Display indicators for stock below minimum thresholds; the database also stores medication movement history.

Data structures supporting clinic services

The portfolio database includes patient profiles with identity details, blood type, allergies, and emergency contacts; vital signs linked to visits; relationships between medical records and visits; and prescriptions with medication details. It also provides JSON change audit logs and analytical views for daily dashboards and stock status.

Foreign keys, unique indexes, check constraints, and timestamps help maintain data consistency. Clinical data relationships restrict deletion to protect records that remain linked. This database structure scope is distinct from the documented interface features.

Demonstration & technology

An optional seeder provides fictional doctors, departments, practice schedules, medication catalogs, and simulated stock for trying the application workflow. It does not add fictional patients, visits, diagnoses, or medical records, and is designed to run repeatedly without duplicating demo data.

PHP 8 runs the application, MySQL stores relational data, Bootstrap supports the interface, and Dompdf generates PDF reports. The project is presented as a portfolio demonstration, without claiming deployment in real clinical services.
